brief: HG spreads retested wides (JULI +4bp to 96bp) after a hot CPI print raised Fed-hike fears and pressured debt-reliant hyperscalers, but Fed-hike odds held at 17% and HG yields fell 22bp WTD, which JPM reads as paradoxically constructive for demand; HG returns recovered half of September's decline and net supply stayed negative. Hyperscaler spreads widened 12bp WoW to 148bp with dispersion rising, yet ratings actually improved despite a $117bn YTD debt increase because new issuance concentrated in higher-rated names, so JPM calls the widening overdone unless earnings show fundamental weakness and favors front-end Financials defensively. On the midterms, JPM's regression finds Fed policy statistically significant for HG spreads (p=0.006) while government control is not (p=0.411), so it argues investors should watch sector-level channels (fiscal/Treasury supply, regulation/M&A, trade policy, consumer affordability) rather than the election outcome; AI infrastructure investment is flagged as durable regardless of result. Separately: 3Q26 ratings upgrades outpaced downgrades 3.1x though agency activity slowed sharply; new-issue underperformance hit its worst level since April 2020; issuer concentration in hyperscalers and banks is rising; and French bank USD spreads screen cheap to JPM's fair-value model.
